overview:
This check monitors [KubeVirt Handler][1] through the Datadog Agent.

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.59.0

[1]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/kubevirt_handler
setup:
Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a host. For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][3] for guidance on applying these instructions.

### Installation

The KubeVirt Handler check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package.
No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Configuration

1. Edit the `kubevirt_handler.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory to start collecting your kubevirt_handler performance data. See the [sample kubevirt_handler.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `kubevirt_handler` under the Checks section.

[3]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/kubernetes/integrations/
[2]: /account/settings/agent/latest
[4]: https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/kubevirt_handler/datadog_checks/kubevirt_handler/data/conf.yaml.example
[5]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#start-stop-and-restart-the-agent
[6]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#agent-status-and-information

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.can_connect
metrics.description: Value of 1 if the agent can connect to the KubeVirt Handler, and 0 otherwise.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.cpu_system_usage_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total CPU time spent in system mode.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.cpu_usage_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total CPU time spent in all modes (sum of both vcpu and hypervisor usage).

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.cpu_user_usage_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total CPU time spent in user mode.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_actual_balloon_bytes
metrics.description: Current balloon size in bytes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_available_bytes
metrics.description: Amount of usable memory as seen by the domain.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_domain_bytes
metrics.description: The amount of memory in bytes allocated to the domain.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_pgmajfault.count
metrics.description: The number of page faults when disk IO was required.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_pgminfault.count
metrics.description: The number of other page faults, when disk IO was not required.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_resident_bytes
metrics.description: Resident set size of the process running the domain.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_swap_in_traffic_bytes
metrics.description: The total amount of data read from swap space of the guest in bytes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_swap_out_traffic_bytes
metrics.description: The total amount of memory written out to swap space of the guest in bytes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_unused_bytes
metrics.description: The amount of memory left completely unused by the system.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.memory_usable_bytes
metrics.description: The amount of memory which can be reclaimed by balloon without pushing the guest system to swap, corresponds to 'Available' in /proc/meminfo

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_receive_bytes.count
metrics.description: Total network traffic received in bytes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_receive_errors.count
metrics.description: Total network received error packets.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_receive_packets.count
metrics.description: Total network traffic received packets.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_receive_packets_dropped.count
metrics.description: The total number of rx packets dropped on vNIC interfaces.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_transmit_bytes.count
metrics.description: Total network traffic transmitted in bytes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_transmit_errors.count
metrics.description: Total network transmitted error packets.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_transmit_packets.count
metrics.description: Total network traffic transmitted packets.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.network_transmit_packets_dropped.count
metrics.description: The total number of tx packets dropped on vNIC interfaces.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.node_cpu_affinity
metrics.description: Number of VMI CPU affinities to node physical cores.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_flush_requests.count
metrics.description: Total storage flush requests.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_flush_times_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total time spent on cache flushing.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_iops_read.count
metrics.description: Total number of I/O read operations.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_iops_write.count
metrics.description: Total number of I/O write operations.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_read_times_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total time spent on read operations.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_read_traffic_bytes.count
metrics.description: Total number of bytes read from storage.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_write_times_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total time spent on write operations.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.storage_write_traffic_bytes.count
metrics.description: Total number of written bytes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.vcpu_delay_seconds.count
metrics.description: Amount of time spent by each vcpu waiting in the queue instead of running.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.vcpu_seconds.count
metrics.description: Total amount of time spent in each state by each vcpu (cpu_time excluding hypervisor time). Where `id` is the vcpu identifier and `state` can be one of the following: [`OFFLINE`, `RUNNING`, `BLOCKED`].

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.vmi.vcpu_wait_seconds.count
metrics.description: Amount of time spent by each vcpu while waiting on I/O.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.adds.count
metrics.description: Total number of adds handled by workqueue

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.depth
metrics.description: Current depth of workqueue

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.longest_running_processor_seconds
metrics.description: How many seconds has the longest running processor for workqueue been running.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.queue_duration_seconds.bucket
metrics.description: How long an item stays in workqueue before being requested.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.queue_duration_seconds.count
metrics.description: How long an item stays in workqueue before being requested.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.queue_duration_seconds.sum
metrics.description: How long an item stays in workqueue before being requested.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.retries.count
metrics.description: Total number of retries handled by workqueue

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.unfinished_work_seconds
metrics.description: How many seconds of work has done that is in progress and hasn't been observed by work_duration. Large values indicate stuck threads. One can deduce the number of stuck threads by observing the rate at which this increases.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.work_duration_seconds.bucket
metrics.description: How long in seconds processing an item from workqueue takes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.work_duration_seconds.count
metrics.description: How long in seconds processing an item from workqueue takes.

metrics.name: kubevirt_handler.workqueue.work_duration_seconds.sum
metrics.description: How long in seconds processing an item from workqueue takes.
